question: Which of the following is a characteristic of sedimentary rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lithification.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition, compaction and cementation of sediments (rock/mineral fragments, organic matter) over long periods. (शैलीकरण — अवसादी शैल)

 

• The process by which loose, unconsolidated sediments are converted into a compact, coherent rock is called lithification. It involves compaction (removal of water/air by pressure) and cementation (binding of grains by minerals like silica, calcite or iron oxide).

 

• Sedimentary rocks are typically found in layers or strata and may contain fossils, e.g. sandstone, limestone, shale.

 

• Lineation, foliation and banding, by contrast, are textures produced by directed pressure and recrystallization and are characteristic of metamorphic rocks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rocks are broadly classified into three types: Igneous (from cooling magma/lava), Sedimentary (from lithification of sediments) and Metamorphic (from transformation of existing rocks under heat and pressure).

 

• Examples of sedimentary rocks include sandstone, shale, limestone and conglomerate.

 

NOTE

 

• Lineation (Option 1): A linear arrangement of mineral grains or structural features, seen in metamorphic rocks, not a defining feature of sedimentary rocks.

 

• Bands (Option 2): Banding (alternating light and dark mineral layers) is a texture typical of metamorphic rocks like gneiss.

 

• Foliation (Option 3): A planar arrangement of mineral grains produced by directed pressure, seen in metamorphic rocks such as slate and schist.

question: Which of the following countries was the host of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is UAE and Oman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021 was jointly hosted by the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Oman, held from 17 October to 14 November 2021. (यूएई और ओमान — टी20 विश्व कप 2021)

 

• The tournament was originally scheduled to be held in India, but was shifted to the UAE and Oman due to the COVID-19 pandemic, though the BCCI remained the official host.

 

• Australia won the title, defeating New Zealand in the final held at Dubai International Cricket Stadium — their first-ever men's T20 World Cup title.

 

• Mitchell Marsh (Australia) was adjudged Player of the Match in the final, and David Warner was named Player of the Tournament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 was subsequently hosted by Australia, and was won by England.

 

• The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 was jointly hosted by the West Indies and the USA.

 

NOTE

 

• West Indies and USA (Option 1): These jointly hosted the 2024 edition, not the 2021 edition.

 

• Australia and New Zealand (Option 2): Australia hosted the 2022 Men's T20 World Cup; New Zealand was not a co-host of any T20 World Cup.

 

• England and Scotland (Option 4): England hosted the 2009 T20 World Cup; this combination did not host the 2021 edition.

question: In rainforests which kind of cultivation is practices?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Slash and burn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Slash-and-burn cultivation is a traditional form of shifting agriculture practised in tropical rainforest regions, where vegetation is cut down and burnt to clear land and enrich the soil with ash before crops are sown. (झूम खेती — वर्षा वन)

 

• After a few years, when soil fertility declines, farmers move to a new patch of forest, allowing the earlier plot to regenerate — hence it is also called shifting cultivation.

 

• In India, this practice is known by different local names: Jhum (North-East India), Podu (Andhra Pradesh/Odisha), Bewar/Dahiya (Madhya Pradesh), and Ponam (Kerala).

 

• It is also widely practised in the rainforests of the Amazon Basin, Central Africa and South-East Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shifting cultivation is considered ecologically damaging when the cycle of land rotation is shortened, leading to deforestation and soil degradation.

 

• In contrast, plantation agriculture (rubber, coffee, oil palm) is a permanent, commercial form of cultivation also common in tropical rainforest regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Dry farming (Option 1): Practised in regions of low rainfall/scanty water availability, relying on soil moisture conservation — the opposite of rainforest conditions.

 

• Vertical farming (Option 2): A modern technique of growing crops in stacked vertical layers, typically in controlled urban environments, unrelated to rainforests.

 

• Terrace farming (Option 3): Practised on steep hill slopes (e.g. in the Himalayas, Western Ghats) to prevent soil erosion, not a defining feature of rainforest cultivation.

question: Who has been elected the 14th Vice President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jagdeep Dhankhar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jagdeep Dhankhar was elected as the 14th Vice President of India in the vice-presidential election held on 6 August 2022, and took oath of office on 11 August 2022. (जगदीप धनखड़ — 14वें उपराष्ट्रपति)

 

• He defeated the opposition's joint candidate Margaret Alva in the election held by the electoral college comprising members of both Houses of Parliament.

 

• Before becoming Vice President, Jagdeep Dhankhar served as the Governor of West Bengal (2019-2022).

 

• As Vice President, he also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jagdeep Dhankhar succeeded M. Venkaiah Naidu, who served as the 13th Vice President of India from 2017 to 2022.

 

• The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, using the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

 

NOTE

 

• Pratibha Banerjee (Option 1): Not a candidate in the 2022 vice-presidential election; this name is a distractor.

 

• Margaret Alva (Option 3): She was the opposition's joint candidate against Jagdeep Dhankhar but lost the election.

 

• Venkaiah Naidu (Option 4): He was the 13th Vice President of India (2017-2022), whom Dhankhar succeeded — not the 14th.

question: In which state is the festival of Gudi Padwa specially celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gudi Padwa is the traditional New Year festival celebrated mainly in Maharashtra, marking the beginning of the Hindu lunar calendar month of Chaitra. (गुड़ी पड़वा — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• It is celebrated by hoisting a 'Gudi' — a bright silk cloth tied atop a bamboo stick with a garland, mango and neem leaves, and an upturned silver/copper vessel — outside homes as a symbol of victory and prosperity.

 

• The festival usually falls in March-April and coincides with Ugadi in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and Cheti Chand among the Sindhi community.

 

• It commemorates the coronation of King Shalivahana and the start of the Shalivahana Shaka calendar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Maharashtra include Ganesh Chaturthi, Nag Panchami and Gokulashtami.

 

• The equivalent New Year festivals in other states are: Ugadi (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana/Karnataka), Baisakhi (Punjab), Poila Boishakh (West Bengal) and Vishu (Kerala).

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 2): The major spring/New Year harvest festival celebrated here is Baisakhi, not Gudi Padwa.

 

• Goa (Option 3): Gudi Padwa is celebrated by some Marathi-speaking communities in Goa, but it is not the state's specially associated festival.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): The traditional New Year festival here is Pana Sankranti (Maha Vishuba Sankranti), not Gudi Padwa.

question: Who among the following became one of the Deputy Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brajesh Pathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brajesh Pathak was sworn in as one of the two Deputy Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh on 25 March 2022, when Yogi Adityanath began his second term as Chief Minister. (ब्रजेश पाठक — उत्तर प्रदेश के उपमुख्यमंत्री)

 

• The other Deputy Chief Minister sworn in alongside him was Keshav Prasad Maurya.

 

• Brajesh Pathak was later given charge of the Health and Family Welfare Department of Uttar Pradesh.

 

• This was the first time Uttar Pradesh had two Deputy Chief Ministers simultaneously in this term of government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yogi Adityanath became the first Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in decades to be re-elected for a consecutive second term, in March 2022.

 

• Keshav Prasad Maurya, the co-Deputy CM, had also served as Deputy CM in the first Yogi Adityanath government (2017-2022).

 

NOTE

 

• Swatantra Dev Singh (Option 2): He was the UP BJP state president and later became a cabinet minister, but was not made Deputy Chief Minister.

 

• Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary (Option 3): He was inducted as a cabinet minister in the Yogi Adityanath government, not as Deputy Chief Minister.

 

• Jayveer Singh (Option 4): He was made a minister of state (independent charge) for Tourism in the UP government, not Deputy Chief Minister.

question: The birthday of Prophet Muhammad is also celebrated by the name of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mawlid al-Nabi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mawlid al-Nabi (also called Eid Milad-un-Nabi in India) marks the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad, observed on the 12th day of Rabi' al-Awwal, the third month of the Islamic calendar. (ईद मिलाद-उन-नबी — पैगंबर मुहम्मद का जन्मदिवस)

 

• The day is marked by processions (Julus), recitation of poetry in praise of the Prophet (Naat), decoration of mosques, and acts of charity.

 

• The word 'Mawlid' literally means 'birth' in Arabic.

 

• It is observed by Muslims across the world, though the manner of observance and its religious significance vary between Sunni and Shia traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, observed with fasting from dawn to dusk, culminating in the festival of Eid-ul-Fitr.

 

• Eid-ul-Adha ('Festival of Sacrifice') commemorates the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son in obedience to God, and coincides with the Hajj pilgrimage.

 

NOTE

 

• Eid-ul-Fitr (Option 1): Marks the end of Ramadan fasting, not the Prophet's birthday.

 

• Ramadan (Option 2): The month of fasting in the Islamic calendar, not a celebration of the Prophet's birth.

 

• Eid-ul-Adha (Option 3): Commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's sacrifice and coincides with Hajj, unrelated to the Prophet Muhammad's birthday.

question:
Which of the following functions of government budget is associated with distribution of income?

I. Allocation function

II. Redistribution function
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Economist Richard Musgrave classified the functions of a government budget into three categories: Allocation function, Distribution (Redistribution) function, and Stabilization function. (पुनर्वितरण कार्य — आय का पुनर्वितरण)

 

• The Redistribution (Distribution) function deals with adjusting the distribution of income and wealth in society, typically through progressive taxation, subsidies and welfare/transfer payments to the poor, to reduce inequality.

 

• The Allocation function, on the other hand, deals with the government's provision of public/social goods (e.g. defence, infrastructure) and correcting market failures — it concerns the efficient allocation of resources, not income distribution.

 

• Since only Statement II (Redistribution function) is associated with distribution of income, 'Only II' is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Stabilization function (the third Musgravian function) aims to maintain economic stability — controlling inflation/deflation, unemployment and ensuring balanced growth through fiscal policy.

 

• Tools of the redistribution function include progressive income tax, subsidies, and social welfare schemes like pensions and public distribution systems.

 

NOTE

 

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, as the Allocation function relates to resource allocation for public goods, not income distribution.

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, as the Redistribution function (II) is indeed associated with distribution of income.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, as only the Redistribution function (II), not the Allocation function (I), deals with income distribution.

question: Identify the correct statement about green algae.
option_1: Green algae usually have a soft cell wall made of an inner layer of pectose.
option_2: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of protein and an outer layer of fibre.
option_3: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.
option_4: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of fat and an outer layer of protein.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Green algae (Chlorophyceae) possess a rigid cell wall composed of two layers — an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose. (हरित शैवाल कोशिका भित्ति — सेल्युलोज व पेक्टोज)

 

• Green algae are photosynthetic, chlorophyll a and b containing organisms, and are considered ancestral to land plants because their cell wall composition (cellulose) resembles that of higher plants.

 

• They store food mainly as starch, similar to plants, and can be unicellular, colonial, or filamentous (e.g. Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra).

 

• The pectose outer layer provides additional structural support and a degree of flexibility to the cell wall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Algae are broadly classified based on pigmentation and stored food into Chlorophyceae (green algae), Phaeophyceae (brown algae) and Rhodophyceae (red algae).

 

• Brown algae cell walls contain cellulose and algin, while red algae cell walls contain cellulose and various polysaccharides including agar.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (soft wall, inner pectose only): Incorrect — the green algal cell wall is rigid, not soft, and has cellulose as the inner layer, not pectose.

 

• Option 2 (inner protein, outer fibre): Incorrect — the layers are not made of protein and fibre; they are cellulose (inner) and pectose (outer).

 

• Option 4 (inner fat, outer protein): Incorrect — fat and protein do not form the structural layers of the green algal cell wall.

question: Dhondo Keshav Karve was an eminent Indian who championed the cause of _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is spread of women education.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhondo Keshav Karve, popularly known as Maharshi Karve, was a great Indian social reformer who devoted his life to the cause of women's education and widow remarriage. (महर्षि धोंडो केशव कर्वे — स्त्री शिक्षा)

 

• He founded the Widow Marriage Association and himself married a widow, and in 1916 he established India's first Women's University, now known as the SNDT Women's University (Shreemati Nathibai Damodar Thackersey Women's University), Mumbai.

 

• He also founded the Hindu Widows' Home Association (1896) at Pune to provide shelter, education and vocational training to widows.

 

• In recognition of his lifelong contribution to social reform and women's education, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1958, at the age of 100.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Maharshi Karve lived for over 100 years (1858-1962) and is remembered as one of the pioneers of the widow remarriage and women's education movements in India.

 

• Other reformers associated with women's education in colonial India include Jyotirao Phule and Savitribai Phule, who started one of the first schools for girls in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Allowing child marriages (Option 1): Incorrect — Karve worked against regressive social practices, not in favour of child marriage.

 

• Prohibiting widow remarriages (Option 2): Incorrect — Karve actively promoted and supported widow remarriage, the opposite of prohibiting it.

 

• Strengthening the caste norms (Option 3): Incorrect — Karve's reform work aimed at breaking rigid social norms, not reinforcing them.

question: Which of the following is potash alum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is K2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.24H2O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Potash alum (Potassium alum) is a double salt with the chemical formula K2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.24H2O, i.e. potassium sulphate and aluminium sulphate crystallised together with 24 molecules of water of crystallisation. (फिटकरी — पोटाश एलम)

 

• It is commonly known as 'Phitkari' in Hindi and is widely used as a water purifier (as a coagulant/flocculant to remove suspended impurities), in styptic pencils to stop minor bleeding, and in the dyeing and tanning industries as a mordant.

 

• Alums in general are double salts of the type M2SO4.M'2(SO4)3.24H2O, where M is a monovalent cation (like K+ or Na+) and M' is a trivalent cation (like Al3+ or Cr3+); potash alum is the most common member of this family.

 

• It crystallises in octahedral crystals and is astringent in taste.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common alum/Potassium alum is used in water treatment plants to make suspended clay/mud particles settle down, making the water clear and fit for further filtration.

 

• Other alums include ammonium alum (NH4)2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.24H2O and chrome alum K2SO4.Cr2(SO4)3.24H2O, used in tanning and dyeing.

 

NOTE

 

• Na2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.24H2O (Option 1): Uses sodium sulphate instead of potassium sulphate, so this is soda alum, not potash alum.

 

• K2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.12H2O (Option 3): The number of water molecules of crystallisation is incorrect — potash alum has 24H2O, not 12H2O.

 

• Na2SO4.Al2(SO4)3.20H2O (Option 4): Incorrect on both counts — it uses sodium sulphate instead of potassium sulphate, and an incorrect number of water molecules (20 instead of 24).

question: Clove is an ______ indicator.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Olfactory.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Olfactory indicators are substances whose smell (odour) changes when mixed with an acidic or a basic solution, allowing them to be used to test the acidic/basic nature of a substance without using colour-changing indicators. (लौंग — घ्राण सूचक)

 

• Clove oil (or crushed cloves) loses its characteristic smell when mixed with a base, making it a classic example of an olfactory indicator.

 

• Other common olfactory indicators include onion, vanilla essence, and freshly cut/crushed onion extract, whose smell also changes/disappears in basic medium.

 

• Unlike acid-base (chemical) indicators such as litmus, phenolphthalein or methyl orange, olfactory indicators are detected by the sense of smell rather than by a colour change.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chemical (acid-base) indicators like litmus, phenolphthalein and methyl orange change colour in acidic or basic media.

 

• A Universal indicator is a mixture of several indicators that gives a range of colours corresponding to different pH values across the entire pH scale.

 

NOTE

 

• Chemical (Option 1): Clove is identified specifically by its smell change, not a colour change like standard chemical/acid-base indicators.

 

• Universal (Option 3): A universal indicator gives a spectrum of colours to indicate pH; clove does not function this way.

 

• Gustatory (Option 4): 'Gustatory' relates to taste, not smell; olfactory indicators like clove are identified by odour, not taste.

question: Which of the following sports was initially known as Poona?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Badminton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sport of Badminton originated in British India, where it was first played by British Army officers stationed in Poona (present-day Pune) in the 1870s, and was initially called 'Poona' or the game of 'Poon-a'. (बैडमिंटन — पूना)

 

• The game was brought to England by retired British officers, who introduced it at Badminton House, the country estate of the Duke of Beaufort in Gloucestershire, England — after which the sport came to be popularly known as Badminton.

 

• The Badminton World Federation (BWF) is the sport's international governing body, headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

 

• Badminton became an Olympic sport in 1992 (Barcelona Olympics).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Famous Indian badminton players include Prakash Padukone, Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal and P.V. Sindhu.

 

• The sport combines elements of an earlier English game called 'Battledore and Shuttlecock' with the Indian game of Poona.

 

NOTE

 

• Baseball (Option 2): Originated in the United States, evolving from older bat-and-ball games like rounders; unrelated to Poona.

 

• Volleyball (Option 3): Invented by William G. Morgan in Massachusetts, USA, in 1895.

 

• Kho-Kho (Option 4): A traditional Indian tag sport, believed to have originated in Maharashtra, but it was never known as 'Poona'.

question: Rajiv Kumar assumed charge as the _______ Chief Election Commissioner of India in May 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajiv Kumar, a retired IAS officer, assumed charge as the 25th Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India on 15 May 2022. (राजीव कुमार — 25वें मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त)

 

• He succeeded Sushil Chandra, who retired as the 24th CEC of India.

 

• Before this appointment, Rajiv Kumar had served as an Election Commissioner and, prior to that, as Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

 

• The Chief Election Commissioner, along with other Election Commissioners, is appointed by the President of India and heads the Election Commission of India, the constitutional body (Article 324) responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Chief Election Commissioner of India was Sukumar Sen, who held office from 1950 to 1958 and conducted India's first general election in 1951-52.

 

• The Election Commission of India was originally a single-member body but became a multi-member body (currently one CEC and two Election Commissioners) since 1993.

 

NOTE

 

• 20th (Option 2): Incorrect ordinal position; Rajiv Kumar was the 25th, not the 20th, CEC.

 

• 27th (Option 3): Incorrect; this overstates his position in the sequence of CECs as of May 2022.

 

• 23rd (Option 4): Incorrect; Sunil Arora was the 23rd CEC of India (2018-2021), preceding Sushil Chandra (24th) and Rajiv Kumar (25th).

question: _____________ was conferred with 'Officier de la Legion d'Honneur', France's highest civilian award, in 2009.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lata Mangeshkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar, known as the 'Nightingale of India', was conferred with the 'Officier de la Legion d'Honneur' (Officer of the Legion of Honour), one of France's highest civilian honours, in 2009. (लता मंगेशकर — लीजन ऑफ ऑनर)

 

• The Legion of Honour (Ordre national de la Legion d'Honneur) is France's highest order of merit, established by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1802, and is awarded for outstanding civil and military contributions.

 

• Lata Mangeshkar was also honoured with India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001, along with the Dada Saheb Phalke Award (1989) and Padma Vibhushan (1999).

 

• She recorded songs in over thirty-six Indian and foreign languages across a career spanning more than seven decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indians conferred with the Legion of Honour include Amitabh Bachchan, Ratan Tata, Shah Rukh Khan and A. R. Rahman.

 

• The Legion of Honour has five ranks in ascending order: Chevalier (Knight), Officier (Officer), Commandeur (Commander), Grand Officier (Grand Officer) and Grand Croix (Grand Cross).

 

NOTE

 

• Asha Bhosale (Option 1): A celebrated playback singer and Lata Mangeshkar's sister, but she was not the recipient of this particular 2009 French honour.

 

• S. Janaki (Option 3): A renowned South Indian playback singer, honoured with the Padma Bhushan, but not the recipient of this French award.

 

• K.S. Chithra (Option 4): A noted South Indian playback singer and Padma Bhushan awardee, but not the recipient of the Legion of Honour in 2009.

question: Who has taken charge as India's new Foreign Secretary in May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinay Mohan Kwatra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vinay Mohan Kwatra, a 1988-batch IFS officer, took charge as India's Foreign Secretary on 29 April 2022. (विनय मोहन क्वात्रा — विदेश सचिव)

 

• He succeeded Harsh Vardhan Shringla, who had served as Foreign Secretary from 2020 to 2022.

 

• Before this appointment, Vinay Mohan Kwatra served as India's Ambassador to Nepal.

 

• The Foreign Secretary is the topmost civil servant and principal adviser in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), responsible for the overall running of the Foreign Service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of External Affairs is headed politically by the External Affairs Minister, a Cabinet-rank minister — Dr. S. Jaishankar held this position at the time.

 

• The Foreign Secretary typically also serves as the Secretary-General of important bilateral/multilateral diplomatic engagements.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajeev Kumar (Option 1): Not the Foreign Secretary in May 2022; this is a distractor name.

 

• T V Somanathan (Option 3): He served as the Finance Secretary of India, not the Foreign Secretary.

 

• Rakesh Mishra (Option 4): Not associated with the position of Foreign Secretary; this is a distractor name.

question: Which of the following region was the capital of the Chalukyas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aihole.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aihole, located in present-day Karnataka, served as an early capital of the Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi) before the capital was shifted to Badami. (ऐहोल — चालुक्य राजधानी)

 

• Aihole is renowned as the 'cradle of Hindu temple architecture', home to over 125 temples built between the 5th and 8th centuries CE, showcasing the early experimentation of Chalukyan temple styles.

 

• The Chalukya dynasty (also called the Chalukyas of Badami/Vatapi) ruled large parts of the Deccan between the 6th and 8th centuries CE, with important centres at Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal — all situated along the Malaprabha river in Karnataka.

 

• Pattadakal, near Aihole, was primarily used as a ceremonial/coronation centre and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site along with the group of monuments at Aihole and Badami.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Durga Temple and Lad Khan Temple at Aihole are notable early examples of Deccan temple architecture.

 

• The Chalukyas of Badami were eventually overthrown by the Rashtrakutas in the mid-8th century CE.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanchipuram (Option 1): This was the capital of the Pallava dynasty, not the Chalukyas.

 

• Raichur (Option 2): A historically contested region between the Vijayanagara Empire and the Bahmani Sultanate (the Raichur Doab), not a Chalukyan capital.

 

• Kolar (Option 4): Known historically for gold mining (Kolar Gold Fields) and ruled at various times by the Gangas and Cholas; not a Chalukyan capital.

question: What is the purpose of the Licensing Policy in India?
option_1: To promote benefits to a particular group
option_2: To maintain the identity of an area
option_3: To show power of the government
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote regional equality.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Industrial Licensing Policy, introduced under the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951, required industrial units to obtain a government licence before setting up or expanding production. (लाइसेंसिंग नीति — क्षेत्रीय समानता)

 

• One of its key objectives was to ensure balanced regional development, i.e. to prevent the concentration of industries in already-developed regions and to promote industrial growth in backward and underdeveloped areas, thereby promoting regional equality.

 

• The policy was part of India's broader framework of planned economic development and state control over the 'commanding heights' of the economy in the pre-1991 era.

 

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991 substantially dismantled the licensing regime (delicensing) as part of India's liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG) reforms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under the 1991 reforms, industrial licensing was retained for only a small list of industries related to security, strategic and environmental concerns.

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (Article 38 and 39) also emphasise reducing regional and income inequalities, which the licensing policy sought to operationalise.

 

NOTE

 

• To promote benefits to a particular group (Option 1): Incorrect — the licensing policy was aimed at broader regional balance, not favouring a particular group.

 

• To maintain the identity of an area (Option 2): Incorrect — this is not an objective of industrial licensing policy.

 

• To show power of the government (Option 3): Incorrect — while licensing did reflect state control over industry, its stated developmental purpose was balanced regional growth, not a display of power.

question: Wood's Despatch is related with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Education.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wood's Despatch, issued in 1854 by Sir Charles Wood, the President of the Board of Control of the East India Company, laid down a comprehensive plan for the spread of education in India. (वुड्स डिस्पैच — शिक्षा)

 

• It is often called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India' as it was the first major statement of British educational policy in India.

 

• It recommended the establishment of universities in Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (which were subsequently founded in 1857), a systematic structure of education from vernacular primary schools to universities, and the establishment of a Department of Public Instruction in each province.

 

• It also recommended grants-in-aid to educational institutions and emphasised education for women and vocational/practical training.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were established in 1857, based on the recommendations of Wood's Despatch, modelled on the University of London.

 

• Earlier, the Macaulay's Minute (1835) had already established English as the medium of higher/official education in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Famine (Option 2): British famine policy is associated with documents like the Famine Codes and various Famine Commissions, not Wood's Despatch.

 

• Trade (Option 3): Colonial trade policy is unrelated to Wood's Despatch, which was specifically an educational policy document.

 

• Military (Option 4): Wood's Despatch did not deal with military affairs; it was concerned exclusively with the reorganisation of education in India.

question: When did the Indian Independence Act receive the British royal assent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is July 1947.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was passed by the British Parliament and received the royal assent on 18 July 1947. (भारतीय स्वतंत्रता अधिनियम — जुलाई 1947)

 

• The Act provided for the partition of British India into two independent dominions — India and Pakistan — effective from 15 August 1947.

 

• It ended British paramountcy over the princely states, giving them the choice to accede to either dominion or remain independent, and abolished the title 'Emperor of India' held by the British monarch.

 

• The Act was based on the recommendations of the Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan, 1947) presented by the last Viceroy, Lord Mountbatten.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India and Pakistan became independent dominions on 15 August 1947, though the Act itself received royal assent about a month earlier, on 18 July 1947.

 

• The Act also empowered India and Pakistan's respective Constituent Assemblies to frame and adopt their own constitutions.

 

NOTE

 

• June 1947 (Option 2): This is when the Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) was announced, proposing partition — not when the Act received royal assent.

 

• May 1947 (Option 3): No major legislative milestone of the Indian Independence Act occurred in May 1947.

 

• August 1947 (Option 4): This is the month India and Pakistan actually became independent (15 August 1947), not when the Act received royal assent (which was in July).

question: Which Indian music director was awarded Japan's Fukuoka prize - 2016 for his outstanding contribution in creating, preserving and showcasing South Asian traditional fusion music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AR Rahman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Renowned Indian music composer A. R. Rahman was awarded the Fukuoka Prize (Arts and Culture Prize) 2016, one of the most prestigious honours from Japan, for his contribution to creating, preserving and showcasing South Asian traditional and fusion music. (ए आर रहमान — फुकुओका पुरस्कार)

 

• The Fukuoka Prize, instituted in 1990 by Fukuoka City, Japan, honours individuals or organisations that have made outstanding contributions to Asian culture in three categories: Grand Prize, Academic Prize and Arts and Culture Prize.

 

• A. R. Rahman, an Academy Award (Oscar), Grammy Award and BAFTA-winning composer, is best known internationally for his score for 'Slumdog Millionaire' (2008).

 

• He is also a recipient of India's Padma Bhushan (2010) and Padma Shri (2000), along with multiple National Film Awards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fukuoka Prize Grand Prize for 2016 was awarded to a different laureate in the Grand Prize/Academic categories, while Rahman received the Arts and Culture Prize.

 

• A. R. Rahman won two Academy Awards in 2009 for 'Slumdog Millionaire' — Best Original Score and Best Original Song ('Jai Ho').

 

NOTE

 

• Vishal Bharadwaj (Option 1): A noted Indian film director and music composer, but he was not the recipient of the Fukuoka Prize 2016.

 

• Pritam Chakraborty (Option 2): A popular Bollywood music composer, not associated with the Fukuoka Prize 2016.

 

• MM Keeravani (Option 4): An acclaimed South Indian composer (later famous for 'Naatu Naatu'/RRR), but not the recipient of this particular award.

question: The official enumeration of population done periodically is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Census.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Census is the official, periodic and complete enumeration of the population of a country, along with the collection, compilation and publication of demographic, economic and social data relating to that population. (जनगणना — जनसंख्या गणना)

 

• In India, the census is conducted every ten years; the first synchronous all-India census was held in 1881, and the most recent complete census was conducted in 2011.

 

• The Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

• Census data covers parameters such as population size, sex ratio, literacy rate, age structure, religion, and occupational pattern, and forms the basis for policy planning, delimitation of constituencies and resource allocation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Census' falls under the Union List of the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, making it the exclusive responsibility of the Central Government.

 

• The 2021 Census of India was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

NOTE

 

• demographic count (Option 2): Not the official/technical term used for this periodic population enumeration exercise.

 

• Estimation (Option 3): An estimation is an approximate calculation, whereas a census is a complete, actual enumeration — not an estimate.

 

• Record (Option 4): A generic term for stored data, not the specific technical term for periodic population enumeration.

question: Chemical formula of bleaching powder is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaOCl2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bleaching powder, chemically known as calcium oxychloride, has the formula CaOCl2, and is also commonly represented as Ca(OCl)Cl. (विरंजक चूर्ण — CaOCl2)

 

• It is manufactured by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime [Ca(OH)2] — a process known as Backmann's process.

 

• Bleaching powder is widely used for bleaching cotton and linen in the textile industry, bleaching wood pulp in paper factories, as an oxidising agent in many chemical industries, and for the disinfection of drinking water.

 

• It has a characteristic strong smell of chlorine and releases chlorine gas slowly on exposure to air.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bleaching powder is used to manufacture chloroform and as a source of available chlorine for oxidation reactions in various industries.

 

• On prolonged storage, bleaching powder loses its available chlorine content and becomes less effective.

 

NOTE

 

• CaO (Option 2): This is the formula for quicklime (calcium oxide), not bleaching powder.

 

• CaCO3 (Option 3): This is the formula for limestone/calcium carbonate, not bleaching powder.

 

• Ca(OH)2 (Option 4): This is the formula for slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), the raw material used to manufacture bleaching powder, not bleaching powder itself.

question: Every law enacted by the government has to be in conformity with the ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the land, and every law enacted by the Union or State legislatures must be in conformity with the Constitution. (संविधान — कानूनों का अनुरूप होना)

 

• Under Article 13 of the Constitution, any law that is inconsistent with or in derogation of the provisions of the Constitution (particularly the Fundamental Rights) is deemed void to the extent of such inconsistency.

 

• The power of judicial review, exercised by the Supreme Court and High Courts, allows courts to strike down any law that violates constitutional provisions.

 

• This principle upholds the doctrine of constitutional supremacy, under which no organ of the state — legislature, executive or judiciary — can act beyond the powers and limits laid down by the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows the concept of 'Constitutional Supremacy', in contrast to countries like the UK, which follow the doctrine of 'Parliamentary Sovereignty'.

 

• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Fundamental Right (Option 1): While laws must not violate Fundamental Rights, this is only one part of the broader requirement of conforming to the entire Constitution.

 

• Directive Principles (Option 2): These are non-justiciable guiding principles (Part IV) for governance, not directly enforceable requirements that every law must conform to.

 

• Preamble (Option 4): The Preamble sets out the objectives and philosophy of the Constitution; laws must conform to the Constitution as a whole, not to the Preamble in isolation.

question: Which of the following is a tree found in Mountain vegetation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chir (Chir Pine, Pinus roxburghii) is a coniferous tree found extensively in mountain/montane vegetation, particularly in the lower Himalayan region at altitudes of about 1000-2000 metres. (चीड़ — पर्वतीय वनस्पति)

 

• Mountain vegetation in India changes with altitude — from deciduous forests at lower elevations, through temperate coniferous forests (chir pine, deodar, oak, blue pine) at middle elevations, to alpine grasslands and scrub near the snowline.

 

• Chir pine is valued commercially for resin, timber and turpentine production.

 

• Other important trees of the temperate Himalayan (mountain) forests include deodar, blue pine (kail), spruce, fir and oak.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alpine vegetation, found at still higher altitudes (above the tree line), consists mainly of grasses, mosses and small shrubs.

 

• India's forest types are broadly classified into Tropical, Montane (Mountain), and Littoral/Swamp forests based on climate and altitude.

 

NOTE

 

• Sundari (Option 1): A characteristic tree of the mangrove/tidal swamp forests of the Sundarbans delta, not mountain vegetation.

 

• Keekar (Option 2): A thorny tree (Acacia nilotica) typically found in dry, arid and semi-arid regions, not montane forests.

 

• Teak (Option 4): A tree of tropical deciduous forests found in regions like Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and peninsular India, not mountain vegetation.
